title: Concurrency: reserved, provisioned and the account limit

videos.script: A function that took a tenth of a second now takes two. The traffic is the same as yesterday. And yet it is being refused. {{law}} The reason is a number Lambda counts that the traffic graph does not show. It is how many requests are running at the same moment. Each one holds an execution environment of its own, and a slow request holds it longer. You will watch the emulator on your own computer refuse a second request it has no room for. {{pool}} Then comes the pool those environments come from. It is a thousand per Region, shared by every function in the account. When it runs out, the caller decides what happens next. Some callers give up, and some retry for hours. {{reserve}} Reserved concurrency carves a piece out of that pool for one function. It protects the function, and it also caps it. That cap is how you keep a database from drowning. {{provision}} Last, provisioned concurrency keeps environments warm before anyone asks. You will price it from the sheet, and in São Paulo the answer is blunt. It never costs less than on demand. You buy it for latency, or you do not buy it.
